WHAT IS A ROBOTICIST?

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]In an era defined by technological advancements, the role of a roboticist has gained prominence. But what exactly is a roboticist? Simply put, a roboticist is a professional specializing in designing, developing, and operating robots. These individuals possess a unique blend of computer science, engineering, and artificial intelligence skills. Roboticists create robots for various applications, from manufacturing and healthcare to space exploration and entertainment. They work with cutting-edge technology, such as machine learning and sensor systems, to imbue robots with intelligence and autonomy. But for me, a creative roboticist is whatever I’d like to make it. Do You Work With Other Roboticists?

Robotics is moving so fast. Much faster than the art world. Oddtoe is there to catch the wake, so to speak, of the incredible work of the robotics community. To work alongside as humanity takes its best guess about how to work with these things. A creative roboticist isn’t the most important cog in this wheel, but I don’t see anyone else looking at making fun of robots, finding ways to let humans feel one last bit of superiority before the machines take our jobs and become our intimate partners ;).

 

What’s the Perfect Piece?

A robot is at the core of the idea. In itself, the robot is so interesting and intricate that I just need to imagine how it could be better, more interesting, how I can bring out features in the robot to the viewer. Could I place the robot in a different setting? Augment it somehow? Color or adorn it? What other forms can be brought to the party — projected light, kinetic sculpture, digital art?

 

What Idea Do I Want the Viewer to Have?

This is my favorite part of the creative process. Robots conjure up so much in the human mind: fascination, curiosity, fear, and I’d like to explore humor. Humor is a circuit breaker and let’s other deeper ideas possible once the viewer has let down their guard. It’s here that exciting possibilities exist, not all of which I can control as an artist. That frees me up to not to have a point to my art ;)

[/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column column_bg_check=”column-background-dark” width=”1/2″ el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ offset=”vc_col-lg-6 vc_col-md-6 vc_col-xs-12″ css=”.vc_custom_1683595641487{padding-right: 0px !important;padding-left: 0px !important;}” col_shadow=”box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)” col_shadow_hover=”box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)”][vc_row_inner css=”.vc_custom_1719801078555{background-image: url(https://www.oddtoe.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Roboticist-Art-Designer-3-jpeg.webp?id=14691) !important;background-position: center !important;background-repeat: no-repeat !important;background-size: cover !important;}”][vc_column_inner]

Plus, a whole lot of human inspiration.

3D & GENERATIVE DESIGN

[/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” dfd_row_parallax=”dfd-row-parallax” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″ css=”.vc_custom_1683596838373{background-color: #252525 !important;}”][vc_column]

I want the robot that eventually pulls the plug on humanity...

…to be adorable, at least.

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″ col_inner_shadow=”box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)” col_inner_shadow_hover=”box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)”]

  • A VISUALIZER WITH TECH EXPERIENCE

    Creative robotics is what your project needs. Get in touch and let’s talk it out.

[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″]

  • The BRIEFS I LIKE

    Three types of projects fit the sweet spot: 3d design, animated stories, and vision work. 

[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″]

  • A ROBOTICIST’s Process

    Yes, form and function and all that. But now the process goes, hand-in-hand, with a robot — a generative AI bot to create what I create.

[/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]
[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner]
[/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_bg_style=”image” dfd_parallax_style=”dfd_vertical_parallax” dfd_bg_image_new=”36″ dfd_bg_image_size=”initial” dfd_parallax_sense=”80″ css=”.vc_custom_1596890262715{background-color: #252525 !important;}”][vc_column width=”1/4″ dfd_column_responsive_enable=”dfd-column-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″]
Ideas as a Designer
[vc_column_text]

Do You Work With Other Roboticists?

Robotics is moving so fast. Much faster than the art world. Oddtoe is there to catch the wake, so to speak, of the incredible work of the robotics community. To work alongside as humanity takes its best guess about how to work with these things. A creative roboticist isn’t the most important cog in this wheel, but I don’t see anyone else looking at making fun of robots, finding ways to let humans feel one last bit of superiority before the machines take our jobs and become our intimate partners ;).

 

What’s the Perfect Piece?

A robot is at the core of the idea. In itself, the robot is so interesting and intricate that I just need to imagine how it could be better, more interesting, how I can bring out features in the robot to the viewer. Could I place the robot in a different setting? Augment it somehow? Color or adorn it? What other forms can be brought to the party — projected light, kinetic sculpture, digital art?

 

What Idea Do I Want the Viewer to Have?

This is my favorite part of the creative process. Robots conjure up so much in the human mind: fascination, curiosity, fear, and I’d like to explore humor. Humor is a circuit breaker and let’s other deeper ideas possible once the viewer has let down their guard. It’s here that exciting possibilities exist, not all of which I can control as an artist. But I love that. Individuals will have individual takes on what I created and what I meant to convey.

That frees me up to not to have a point to my art 😉

[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” css=”.vc_custom_1787200000002{background-color: #252525 !important;}”][vc_column width=”1/4″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″]
[vc_column_text css=”” item_animation=”transition.fadeIn”]

Questions & Answers

Creative Robotics

[/vc_column_text]

[dfd_accordion style=”style-3″ active_section=”1″ font_size=”18″ tab_title_google_fonts=”yes” tab_title_custom_fonts=”font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal” icon_size=”14″][vc_tta_section title=”What is a roboticist?” tab_id=”faqrobo-1-2026″][vc_column_text css=””]

A professional who specialises in designing, developing and operating robots, combining engineering, computer science and artificial intelligence. Roboticists build robots for everything from manufacturing and research to entertainment and public installations.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”What does a creative roboticist do?” tab_id=”faqrobo-2-2026″][vc_column_text css=””]

A creative roboticist works on how a robot looks, moves and reads to an audience, not only on whether it functions. Oddtoe designs and prototypes robots using kits and generative AI, which gets to a working prototype far faster than building every part from scratch.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Who hires a creative roboticist?” tab_id=”faqrobo-3-2026″][vc_column_text css=””]

Tech companies, film productions, museums, start-ups, advertising agencies and futurists — usually when a robot has to be seen by an audience rather than just work on a factory floor.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Is a roboticist the same as a robotics engineer?” tab_id=”faqrobo-4-2026″][vc_column_text css=””]

Not quite. A robotics engineer is usually focused on mechanics, electronics and control systems. Roboticist is the broader term and takes in design, behaviour and application as well. Oddtoe works on the design and prototyping side.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html]
